clue.text: Hope and Crosby featured in short reel

parts.note: Bob Hope, the comedian of the Road films

indicators.note: short means the name loses its final letter, as if cut off

parts.note: Bing Crosby, Hope's singing partner in the Road films

explanation.surface: Two old film stars appear together in a brief bit of film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims BING to BIN; 'reel' looks like film but is the definition, a spool for thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobbin is a spool or cylinder on which thread is wound, a kind of reel.

clue.text: Investment in one of next generation of spies?

definitions.meaning: a savings scheme set up for a newborn child

definitions.text: one of next generation of spies?
definitions.meaning: a child of the famous fictional agent 007, whimsically

explanation.surface: Someone puts money into training a young secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby bond was a UK tax-free savings plan for children; the second reading is an infant offspring of James Bond.

clue.text: Exotic island adopts English language

indicators.note: adopts means the island takes the abbreviation into itself, holding it inside

parts.note: Bali, the Indonesian holiday island

explanation.surface: A far-off island takes on English as its tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali is the language of Bangladesh and West Bengal, a specific tongue fitting the generic word.

clue.text: Naughty child and dunce disconcerted head of English … showing this?

definitions.text: Naughty child and dunce disconcerted head of English … showing this?

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: disconcerted means thrown into confusion, so the letters of dunce are jumbled
head of signals taking only the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A cheeky pupil and a dim one upset the head of the English department with their cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disconcerted' turns DUNCE into UDENC. The whole clue also describes the cheek such pupils show to a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudence is cheeky disrespect, exactly what a naughty child and a dunce rattling a head of department would display.

clue.text: Trousers bound to be given to workers

parts.note: to bound is to leap or skip
worker ants: crossword shorthand for workers

explanation.surface: Jumping is required of the labour force.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski pants are close-fitting trousers worn for skiing.

clue.text: Nasty strike looming? Labour leader called in foreign policy specialist

indicators.note: something nasty is in a bad state, so these letters are scrambled
leader means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A threatening industrial strike is coming, and the Labour leader brings in an expert on overseas affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty strike looming' reads as industrial unrest; 'called in' adds the Labour leader's letter to the pool before the jumble, and 'foreign policy specialist' is a Cold War Moscow-watcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Kremlinology was the Cold War study of Soviet policy, so its practitioner is a foreign-affairs analyst.

clue.text: Draws good reviews

definitions.meaning: draws on a cigarette or pipe, inhales

explanation.definitionFit: Puffs are drags on a cigarette, and also flattering promotional write-ups.

clue.text: Middle of the day, and ailing horse gets in shape

indicators.note: gets in means the horse is placed inside the time of day

parts.note: noon is midday
a nag is a worn-out, broken-down horse

explanation.surface: At midday a sick horse gets into condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in shape' reads as getting fit, but 'shape' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a plane figure with nine sides, a geometric shape.

clue.text: Pirate treasure

definitions.meaning: Long John, the buccaneer in Treasure Island
a precious metal, or valuable tableware made of it

explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver is Stevenson's pirate, and silver is a valuable metal treasured as plate.

clue.text: Left in grip of plague: one country's fate

indicators.note: in grip of means one word is held inside another

parts.note: a pest is an old word for plague or pestilence
red means left-wing politically
I is the Roman numeral for one
a nation is a country; the 's is a link meaning has

explanation.surface: A left-winger is caught by disease, and a nation's destiny follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Predestination is the doctrine that one's destiny is fixed beforehand.

clue.text: One accepts a role assigned to British leader

indicators.note: accepts means the word takes other letters inside it

parts.note: taken as written
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a job given to a British commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' at the end, after 'British', looks like part of the wordplay but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was the French emperor and military leader.

clue.text: Like one's journey to cemetery in coffin alas

indicators.note: in signals the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Sadly describing the last trip to the graveyard in a casket.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip to the grave is the last journey anyone makes, so it is described as the ultimate one.

clue.text: Helped by brother, put hair into plaits

parts.note: aided means helped

explanation.surface: A sibling assisted in doing someone's hair in plaits.
explanation.definitionFit: Braided means woven into plaits, past tense matching the verb phrase.

clue.text: Dish with herb chopped in a certain way

indicators.note: in shows the shortened herb sitting inside the road

parts.note: a lane is a particular kind of way or road

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: sage is a kitchen herb

explanation.surface: A recipe has a herb chopped in a specific manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' wants to be an anagram signal; here it docks SAGE to SAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is an Italian baked pasta dish.

clue.text: Town rebuilt in Northern Iran

indicators.note: rebuilt means put together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A town is reconstructed in the north of a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: NAIRN is a town on the Moray Firth in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairn is a small town in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Deposit shilling with financial institution

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin
and means with
a bank is a financial institution

explanation.surface: Someone pays a shilling into the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin, abbreviated s. 'Deposit' looks like a money verb but is the noun for silt laid down.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandbank is a ridge of sand laid down by water, a natural deposit.

clue.text: Entering club, woman's removed top … displaying this?

definitions.text: Entering club, woman's removed top … displaying this?

indicators.note: entering means the trimmed word goes inside the golf club name

parts.note: a brassie is an old golf club, a wooden two-wood

indicators.note: removed top means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman takes her top off on arriving at the club, revealing her underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed top' turns HER into ER. Read whole, the clue shows what a woman who has taken off her top would display.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere is a bra, what would be on show once the top came off.

clue.text: Maybe small shopkeeper mentioned place to store wine

indicators.note: mentioned means the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a seller-ette, a little seller, whimsically coined

explanation.surface: Perhaps a modest retailer spoke of somewhere to keep bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: The '-ette' diminutive on 'seller' gives a small seller, which spoken matches the wine cabinet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellaret is a cabinet or sideboard for storing bottles of wine.

clue.text: Move slowly down where battle was fought

parts.note: to edge is to move gradually or cautiously
a down is a rolling chalk hill in southern England

explanation.surface: Creep slowly downhill to the site of a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like a direction but is a noun: the English downs are low grassy hills.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgehill in Warwickshire was the site of the first major battle of the English Civil War in 1642.

clue.text: American in country uprising left with nothing

indicators.note: in places one item inside the reversed word
uprising in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: land means country

explanation.surface: An American in a country in revolt is left with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' reads the country upwards, as this is a down clue, and the American abbreviation sits inside it; 'uprising' suggests revolt in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Damn all is a slangy, emphatic way of saying nothing whatsoever.

clue.text: Intense rancour they regularly displayed

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Bitter ill feeling was shown by them often.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute means intense or severe, as in acute pain.

clue.text: Where Spooner's rabbit is accommodated for free?

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: in names the place where something is
a hutch is a cage where a pet rabbit lives

explanation.surface: Asking where a rabbit can be housed without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in hutch', with the sounds swapped, says 'un hitch'. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhitch is to unfasten or set loose, so to free.

clue.text: Not just heartless ruffian that's in need of reform

indicators.note: in need of reform means the letters must be reorganised into another form
heartless means the central letter is removed

explanation.surface: An unprincipled thug must be made to mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle F out of RUFFIAN, leaving RUFIAN to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair means unjust, so not just in the moral sense.

clue.text: Chap withdrawing, last character to leave island for country in Africa

indicators.note: withdrawing means drawing back, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: a man is a chap

indicators.note: last character to leave means the final letter of the alphabet is removed

parts.note: Ibiza is a Spanish Balearic island

explanation.surface: A man pulls out and the final person leaves an island to go to Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last character' means Z, the final letter of the alphabet, not the island's last letter (which happens to be A).
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is a country in south-west Africa.

clue.text: Thick, unkempt policeman astride horse

indicators.note: astride means the word sits either side of the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: busy is old slang for a detective or policeman
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: A dim, scruffy constable sits on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is slang for heroin, abbreviated H; 'busy' is British slang for a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushy describes hair or growth that is thick and shaggy.

clue.text: Fuel — several litres needed when touring part of London

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the measure surrounds the district

parts.note: a gallon, abbreviated GAL, is about four and a half litres
Soho is a district of London's West End

explanation.surface: A lot of petrol is needed for driving round a London district.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasohol is a fuel blending petrol with alcohol.

clue.text: US President, first man at opening of Senate

parts.note: Adam was the first man in Genesis

indicators.note: opening of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A President is the first to arrive when the Senate opens.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and John Quincy Adams were both Presidents of the United States.

clue.text: Policeman in area with limited parking

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: limited means the area hems in the parking letter

parts.note: a sector is an area or zone
P is the symbol for parking

explanation.surface: An officer is in a zone where parking is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is a police officer ranking above sergeant.

clue.text: Joining forces with Resistance, so making recovery

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
allying means joining forces

explanation.surface: Teaming up with the Resistance movement, so getting back on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' suggests the wartime underground; it is R from physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallying means recovering strength, as markets or patients rally.

clue.text: Burning with enthusiasm?

parts.note: hot with fervour as well as literally glowing from heat

explanation.definitionFit: Red-hot means glowing with heat, and figuratively intensely keen or passionate.
